title: Minimum Number of Operations to Satisfy Conditions
summary: Given a matrix, determine the least number of operations required to ensure each cell matches the one directly below it and differs from the cell to its right.
statement: Given a matrix, determine the least number of operations required to ensure each cell matches the one directly below it and differs from the cell to its right.
constraints: grid is a nonempty rectangular matrix whose values are digits zero through nine.
Every column must become constant from top to bottom, and horizontally adjacent columns must use different digits.
One operation changes one cell; return the minimum operations.
hints: Vertical equality means each column chooses one digit; horizontal inequality couples only adjacent column choices.
Count digit frequencies per column and run DP over the ten possible previous digits.
The local change cost is exact for a constant column, and the transition enforces precisely the only cross-column condition.
editorial: The local change cost is exact for a constant column, and the transition enforces precisely the only cross-column condition.

tests.explanation: Columns are already constant and neighboring digits differ, so zero operations are needed.
Choosing column digits one and zero changes one cell in each column, for two operations.
